Description: As a Kimi Code user, I want Maestro to delegate tasks to the `kimi` CLI so that I can use Kimi K3 as the model.
Acceptance Criteria: A `kimi-cli` runtime exists; it spawns the `kimi` CLI with the correct model flag and returns parsed output.

Description: As a Claude Code user, I want Maestro to delegate tasks to the `claude` CLI so that I can keep using Claude agents.
Acceptance Criteria: A `claude-cli` runtime exists; it passes `--model`, `--allowedTools`, and `--mcp-config` as appropriate.

Description: As a user, I want an API-only runtime so Maestro can run in CI, cloud, or with local OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
Acceptance Criteria: The `openai-sdk` runtime implements a full tool loop and honors `allowed_tools`/`blocked_tools`.

Description: As a Claude user, I want an in-process SDK runtime that can intercept tool calls.
Acceptance Criteria: The `claude-sdk` runtime uses `claude-agent-sdk` and supports `can_use_tool` callbacks.

Description: As a Kimi user, I want the Agent Client Protocol runtime so Maestro can request permissions per tool call.
Acceptance Criteria: The `kimi-acp` runtime exists and wires ACP `request_permission` callbacks to tool guards.

Description: As a user, I want to add/override models in a YAML registry so Maestro can use new providers without code changes.
Acceptance Criteria: `~/.open-maestro/capabilities.yaml` and `.open-maestro/capabilities.yaml` are loaded and override defaults.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to match task requirements (reasoning, coding, vision, context) to model capabilities.
Acceptance Criteria: The router excludes models that cannot meet hard requirements and scores the rest by fit, cost, and latency.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to pick the cheapest capable model for each task.
Acceptance Criteria: `--cost-preference low` and inferred cost preference influence the selected model.

Description: As a user, I want `--prefer-local` to prefer Ollama/vLLM when available.
Acceptance Criteria: `--prefer-local` filters candidates to `provider: ollama`/`local` and probes `OLLAMA_HOST` automatically.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to refresh its static cost ranking periodically with live provider pricing.
Acceptance Criteria: A scheduled job (default weekly) fetches public price APIs and updates `relative_cost` values.

Description: As a user, I want the cheapest model to be skipped if it is more than 20%% slower than the fastest alternative.
Acceptance Criteria: Measured tokens-per-second from `latency.yaml` is used to enforce a configurable latency tolerance.

Summary: Markdown agent definitions with YAML frontmatter
Description: As an agent author, I want agents defined in Markdown so they are human-readable and version-controllable.
Acceptance Criteria: Agents load from `.md` files with `id`, `role`, `model`, `tools`, `skills`, and `required_capabilities`.

Description: As a user, I want project agents to override user agents, which override bundled agents.
Acceptance Criteria: `AgentLoader.load_tiered_dirs` resolves project → user → bundled precedence.

Description: As an agent author, I want agents to extend a base agent so I can avoid duplication.
Acceptance Criteria: The `extends` field merges scalar fields, tool lists, skills, and capabilities.

Description: As a user, I want to add skills at the project or user level so agents can use custom instructions.
Acceptance Criteria: Skills load from `./.open-maestro/skills/`, `~/.open-maestro/skills/`, and bundled `skills/`.

Description: As a team lead, I want Maestro to sync agents/skills from a Git repo so the team shares a single source of truth.
Acceptance Criteria: `maestro --add-agent-source`/`--add-skill-source` clones/updates Git repositories into `~/.open-maestro/sources/`.

Description: As a user, I want the MIT claude-mpm-skills repo available by default on first run.
Acceptance Criteria: The default `sources.yaml` includes `claude-mpm-skills` and syncs it automatically.

Description: As a user behind a firewall, I want bundled agents/skills to work without internet.
Acceptance Criteria: The wheel ships 15 bundled agents and 174 bundled skills; sync warnings are suppressed when offline.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to include the 47+ specialist agents from claude-mpm.
Acceptance Criteria: At least 30 additional specialist agents (frontend, backend, security, DevOps, QA) are bundled or sourced.

Description: As a user, I want each project to have its own persistent memory database.
Acceptance Criteria: `KuzuMemoryClient` binds to `cwd` and calls `kuzu-memory init` if no DB exists.

Description: As a user, I want semantic code search before delegation so agents get relevant code context.
Acceptance Criteria: `--search` recalls results from `mcp-vector-search` and includes them in the orchestration context.

Description: As a user, I want MCP servers to be discovered and passed to the correct runtime.
Acceptance Criteria: MCP config is loaded from project/user/env/flag; `claude-cli` gets `--mcp-config`, `openai-sdk` spawns stdio tools.

Description: As a user, I want to restrict which tools an agent can use.
Acceptance Criteria: `--allowed-tools`, `--block-tools`, agent `blocked_tools`, and SDK tool guards are enforced.

Description: As a user, I want a read-only mode that denies mutating tools.
Acceptance Criteria: `--permission-mode read-only` and `--deny-dangerous` are implemented across runtimes.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to warn me as context usage grows.
Acceptance Criteria: `ContextMonitor` tracks cumulative tokens and returns `warning`/`critical` at configured thresholds.

Description: As a user, I want a concise resume log when context pressure is critical.
Acceptance Criteria: `build_resume_log()` produces a markdown summary of progress, decisions, and next steps.

Description: As a user, I want to continue or branch a previous session.
Acceptance Criteria: `--resume` lists/reloads sessions; `--fork` copies a session under a new ID.

Description: As a user, I want to stay in one interactive session across multiple prompts.
Acceptance Criteria: `maestro --interactive` runs a `while True` loop until `/exit` or Ctrl-C.

Summary: Standard terminal line editing in interactive mode
Description: As a user, I want backspace and arrow keys to work normally in interactive mode.
Acceptance Criteria: readline is configured; reported issues with `^C` on backspace and `^[[A` on arrow keys remain.

Description: As a user, I want to know what step is running while I wait.
Acceptance Criteria: `ProgressIndicator` and event-bus handlers print `Thinking`, elapsed time, and step labels.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to infer `--reasoning`/`--fast` from plain English so I do not type flags.
Acceptance Criteria: `TaskProfiler.from_prompt` infers reasoning, coding strength, vision, and urgency from text.

Description: As a user, I want to inspect the execution plan before spending tokens.
Acceptance Criteria: `--show-plan` and `/plan`/`/dry` print selected runtime, model, and agent without calling the LLM.

Description: As a user, I want the PM to hand a task from a researcher to an engineer automatically.
Acceptance Criteria: `_run_with_handoff` exists but fails when the runtime does not support tool interception (e.g., `claude-cli`).

Summary: Artifact output routing to project folders
Description: As a user, I want generated docs to land in `docs/`, `requirements/`, `scripts/`, or `tests/`.
Acceptance Criteria: The orchestrator instructs agents to save outputs to conventional subfolders.

Description: As a user, I want to see which vendor and model produced each response.
Acceptance Criteria: Each turn prints `Vendor: ... / Model: ... / Runtime: ...` at the end of output.

Description: As a user, I want to type natural language tasks without memorizing CLI syntax.
Acceptance Criteria: Any non-slash input is treated as a task; flags and runtime are inferred automatically.

Description: As a user, I want milestone state stored in a project-scoped YAML file.
Acceptance Criteria: `MilestoneStore` reads/writes `.open-maestro/milestones.yaml` with Pydantic models.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to infer milestone status from existing project files.
Acceptance Criteria: `MilestoneDetector` scans artifact patterns (docs/blueprint*, tests/fixtures/, etc.) per milestone.

Description: As a user, I want `/milestones`, `/next`, `/complete`, `/blocker`, and `/track` commands.
Acceptance Criteria: All five slash commands are implemented and update local YAML state.

Description: As a user, I want agents to know the current milestone and exit criteria.
Acceptance Criteria: `format_prompt_context()` injects current milestone, completion, and exit criteria into prompts.

Description: As a user, I want to export a client-safe progress view.
Acceptance Criteria: `--export-dashboard json|markdown|html` writes the dashboard to stdout/file.

Description: As a user, I want to serve the dashboard from Maestro for local review.
Acceptance Criteria: `--serve-dashboard` runs an HTTP server on a configurable host/port.

Description: As a user, I want to publish the dashboard to `merven.ai` from the CLI.
Acceptance Criteria: `--publish-dashboard <url>` POSTs JSON with API key and project token.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to pull the canonical milestone plan from Merven.
Acceptance Criteria: `--sync-milestones` fetches the plan from the Merven API and overwrites local YAML.

Summary: Dashboard styled with merven.ai design tokens
Description: As a user, I want the HTML dashboard to match the merven.ai brand.
Acceptance Criteria: HTML uses `#02040b` background, `#00bfaf` accent, Inter font, gradient cards.

Summary: Epic swimlanes with milestone Gantt charts
Description: As a user, I want epics as rows and their 8 milestones as Gantt bars.
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard renders epic swimlanes with two rows of four milestones each.

Description: As a user, I want completed/in-progress/blocked badges to be readable.
Acceptance Criteria: Status badges and Gantt bars use high-contrast solid colors and text shadows.

Description: As a user, I want each Maestro project to have its own client dashboard.
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard payload is keyed by project ID/token; Merven stores per-project dashboard state.

Description: As a team lead, I want a pre-built wheel to share with engineers.
Acceptance Criteria: `python -m build --wheel` produces `open_maestro-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl`.

Description: As a team lead, I want engineers to install Maestro with one command.
Acceptance Criteria: `scripts/install-ubuntu.sh` creates venv, installs wheel, and symlinks `maestro`.

Description: As a user on a firewalled machine, I want to install Maestro without internet.
Acceptance Criteria: Wheel + `pip install --no-index --find-links .` workflow documented and tested on WSL.

Summary: Bundle kuzu-memory and mcp-vector-search in install
Description: As a user, I want the install script to optionally install memory/search dependencies.
Acceptance Criteria: `install-ubuntu.sh` supports flags/env vars for optional extras.

Description: As a team lead, I want a guide for distributing Maestro to engineers.
Acceptance Criteria: `docs/DEPLOY.md` covers wheel distribution, install script, backends, MCP, troubleshooting.

Description: As a user, I want a documented way to wipe and reinstall the venv while keeping config.
Acceptance Criteria: `docs/DEPLOY.md` includes in-place upgrade and nuclear force-reinstall instructions.

Description: As a user, I want a live view of the current agent, runtime, model, and task state while Maestro runs.
Acceptance Criteria: `maestro --monitor` shows a Rich live panel with agent, runtime, model, task, context, and recent events.

Description: As a user or team lead, I want a running log of features released with each version.
Acceptance Criteria: `CHANGELOG.md` documents major/minor releases from 1.0.0 through 1.3.0.

Description: As a maintainer, I want Maestro source code in a remote GitHub repo so it is not only on one machine.
Acceptance Criteria: Repository created at https://github.com/mervenai/open-maestro with initial commit of v1.3.0.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want the orchestrator to decompose my request into a sequence of agent steps so that complex tasks are handled by the right specialists in the right order.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a prompt like 'implement the budget import feature', when the planner runs, then it outputs a chain of 2-5 steps with explicit agent_id and purpose for each. Given a simple prompt like 'summarize this file', when the planner runs, then it returns a single-step chain. Given an unknown agent name returned by the LLM, when the chain is validated, then it is replaced with the closest matching registered agent or the default engineer.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want the planned agent chain to run automatically without manual approval so that I can delegate complex workflows in one prompt.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a multi-step plan, when execution starts, then each agent runs only after the previous agent completes successfully. Given a step produces an error, when the chain executor detects it, then the chain stops and returns the error with a summary of completed steps. Given all steps complete, when the final step finishes, then the orchestrator returns a synthesized result containing outputs from every step.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want the chain to be capped at 5 agents so that token cost and runtime stay bounded.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the planner returns more than 5 steps, when the chain is validated, then it is truncated to 5 steps with a warning logged. Given the chain reaches 5 completed steps, when the executor checks for dynamic expansion, then no additional agents are added.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want to see each agent's full output grouped under its name so that I can trace who did what.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a 3-agent chain completes, when the final response is rendered, then it contains clearly labeled sections like '## Researcher', '## Engineer', '## QA'. Given a single-step execution, when the result is returned, then it is formatted exactly as before with no extra grouping headers.

Description: As a Maestro operator, I want each agent in the chain to use the cheapest capable model available so that complex chains remain cost-effective.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a chain step requires deep reasoning, when the model is selected, then a reasoning-capable model is chosen using the existing select_runtime_for_task logic. Given two models satisfy a step's profile, when costs are compared, then the cheaper model is selected. Given a step requires tool use, when a local cheap model lacks tool support, then it is excluded even if it is cheapest.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want common workflows like 'implement a feature' to have predefined chains so that the LLM planner has reliable defaults and does not hallucinate.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a prompt classified as feature_implementation, when the planner runs, then it uses the predefined chain [research, engineer, qa] unless the LLM overrides with justification. Given a prompt classified as technical_analysis, when the planner runs, then it uses the predefined chain [research, documentation]. Given a prompt does not match any predefined pattern, when the planner runs, then it falls back to LLM-driven decomposition.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want the existing read-only to writer handoff to remain available so that simple writing tasks still work when chaining is disabled.
Acceptance Criteria: Given --chain is not passed and the selected agent is read-only, when the task requires writing, then the existing _run_with_handoff logic executes. Given --chain is passed, when the task can be decomposed, then the multi-agent chain executes instead of the 2-step handoff. Given --chain is passed but the planner returns a single step, when execution starts, then it behaves like a normal single-agent turn.

Description: As a Maestro user running with --monitor, I want the live monitor to show the current chain step and agent so that I can observe multi-agent progress in real time.
Acceptance Criteria: Given --monitor --chain is active, when a new step starts, then the monitor displays 'step 2/4: engineer'. Given a step completes, when the monitor refreshes, then the recent activity includes the completed step's agent name.

Description: As a Maestro interactive user, I want to toggle chaining mode with /chain so that I can enable or disable multi-agent behavior per session.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the user types /chain in interactive mode, when the command is processed, then chaining is toggled and the current state is printed. Given chaining is enabled, when the user submits a prompt, then the planner runs before agent execution. Given chaining is disabled, when the user submits a prompt, then the existing single-agent behavior runs.

Description: As an interactive user, I want Kimi/Claude CLI subprocess output streamed to the terminal in real time with Rich formatting, so that I can see actual tool calls and progress during a turn instead of only an elapsed-time heartbeat.
Acceptance Criteria: CLI runtime stdout/stderr streams live during turns (v1.5.1) and renders with colored [kimi]/[claude] labels, stream-json decoded into readable content/tool lines (v1.5.2).

Description: As a project lead, I want a built-in milestone prompt playbook with /next suggestions and /prompts listing, so that I can run a proven intake-to-retrospective process without writing prompts from scratch.
Acceptance Criteria: The bundled software-consulting playbook ships prompt templates for all 8 lifecycle milestones with {date}/{epic_id}/{artifact_target} placeholders and project-level overrides via .open-maestro/playbook.yaml; /next suggests the top 3 prompts and /prompts lists all (v1.5.0, later: [Ran] backfill from artifacts v1.8.4, auto-advance to in_progress v1.8.3, agent_hint honored without an LLM routing call v3.0.0).

Description: As an interactive user, I want to select suggested prompts through a cursor-driven checkbox TUI with inline editing and multi-select queueing, so that I can review, tweak, and run several prompts in one step.
Acceptance Criteria: Typing a number or /select opens a questionary checkbox TUI showing full prompt bodies; selections can be edited inline or in $EDITOR and are queued for sequential execution (v1.5.4-v1.6.5, settled v1.6.5).

Description: As a project lead, I want a per-project todo list with /todo add/list/done/block/delete/clear commands, so that in-flight work is tracked and specialists know what is already underway.
Acceptance Criteria: Todos persist in .open-maestro/todos.json and open todos are automatically injected into each agent's system prompt (v1.7.0).

Description: As a project stakeholder, I want milestone dashboards published to a standalone receiver or Supabase so that remote frontends render live project status without the Merven project.
Acceptance Criteria: maestro --serve-remote-dashboard accepts published snapshots and serves JSON/HTML/Markdown by project token (v1.8.0); maestro --publish-dashboard supabase upserts into maestro_dashboards with a generated per-project token and public render URL (v1.14.0); the interactive banner shows the last publish time and URL (v1.8.3).

Description: As a project lead running multi-epic projects, I want work epics auto-populated from the epic breakdown with per-epic status rollup, so that the dashboard and /next tracks reflect real epic progress.
Acceptance Criteria: Marking Intake complete auto-creates a work epic with the 8 lifecycle milestones parsed from docs/intake/epics.md (CE-n numbering supported, v1.8.9/1.20.3); the dashboard derives a 3-step epic tracker (Planning/In Progress/Complete) from the highest active milestone (v1.8.7-1.9.1); project-wide prompts are tagged default_track_only and non-applicable phases scaffold as SKIPPED (v1.20.4/1.20.5).

Description: As a cost-conscious user, I want registered local Ollama models with a /local preference mode and approval-gated escalation, so that routine work stays cheap and private while frontier models require my consent.
Acceptance Criteria: ollama-qwen2-5-coder-32b (local-smart) and ollama-deepseek-coder-v2 (local-reasoning) are registered and consumed through the openai-sdk runtime via Ollama's endpoint (v1.9.3); /local toggles local preference and --ask-escalate starts with approval-before-frontier-switch behavior (v1.9.5).

Description: As an interactive user, I want a deterministic /status (alias /where) command, so that I can see where the project left off without spending tokens on an LLM answer.
Acceptance Criteria: /status renders milestone progress with current/next milestone and active blockers, the last 5 sessions with agent and model, and any resume-log handoff, directly from disk with no LLM call (v1.18.0).

Description: As an interactive user, I want real multi-line editing with persistent history and bold colored prompts, so that drafting and recalling long prompts matches claude-cli/kimi-cli ergonomics.
Acceptance Criteria: Enter submits while Ctrl+J/Alt+Enter inserts newlines, arrow keys traverse multi-line drafts, and history persists across sessions via prompt_toolkit FileHistory (v1.18.1); typed prompts render bold amber with a MAESTRO_PROMPT_COLOR override and dim turn separators (v1.21.1).

Description: As a security reviewer, I want an impl-005 security scan gate running secrets/SAST/dependency/SBOM tools with a GO/NO-GO verdict, so that milestones cannot exit with unaddressed critical findings.
Acceptance Criteria: The software-consulting playbook's impl-005 runs gitleaks, semgrep, npm/pip audit, and syft CycloneDX SBOM, records missing tools as skips never failures, and makes a clean scan report an implementation exit criterion (v1.12.0); the security-scanning skill's scan-gate section codifies the exact commands, report shape, and verdict vocabulary (v3.0.0).

Description: As a team lead, I want implementation turns that change significant code to trigger an automatic code-critic review with an APPROVE/WARN/BLOCK verdict, so that low-quality changes are caught before I accept the result.
Acceptance Criteria: Turns changing more than 50 code lines or 1 source file run an automatic code-critic pass whose verdict and top findings are appended to the result (metadata critic_verdict); disable via --no-critic-gate or MAESTRO_CRITIC_GATE=off (v1.13.0).

Description: As an operator, I want models to declare their own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, API-key env var, and per-million pricing, so that cost estimates are real and providers don't collide on global config.
Acceptance Criteria: Registry entries support per-model endpoint/api_key_env overrides (v1.15.0) and price_input/output_per_million, and the openai-sdk runtime computes cost_usd on AgentResult (v1.15.2); endpoint-less cloud models require generic OPENAI_API_KEY and Alibaba qwen entries declare their DashScope endpoint (v1.16.4).

Description: As a cost-conscious operator, I want a cheap cloud fast tier with per-model endpoints that rotates as providers die, so that routine tasks route to inexpensive models and degrade gracefully.
Acceptance Criteria: glm-5-3-flash was registered as the fast alias with its own ZAI_API_KEY endpoint (v1.15.0); deepseek-flash (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, tool_use corrected v2.1.9) joined the adversarial panel as the causal-auditor seat (v2.1.6); GLM was retired and deepseek-flash inherited the fast alias with the panel skeptic seat passing to GPT-4o mini (v3.0.4).

Description: As a project lead, I want playbook prompts to re-verify intake claims, audit story coverage, and record spec deviations, so that wrong assumptions don't propagate silently into implementation.
Acceptance Criteria: plan-001 re-verifies load-bearing intake claims against the actual repos, design-003 audits FR/measurable-target/open-question coverage before finishing, build-002's matrix covers targets and NFRs, and impl-001/002/003 must read the frozen specs and log contradictions to docs/spec-deviations.md (v1.16.3).

Description: As a user of streaming providers, I want the runtime to retry transient failures, tolerate long silent streams, compact over-length prompts once, and nudge the model near its turn cap, so that turns survive real-world provider behavior.
Acceptance Criteria: Streaming requests retry up to 3 attempts with a 30-minute default read window instead of httpx's 600s (v1.16.1); length-related 400s trigger a one-time conversation compaction and retry (v1.16.7); at roughly 75% of the tool-turn cap a system message tells the model to stop exploring and produce its final artifact (v1.16.6).

Description: As a Maestro user, I want tasks with 3+ independent targets fanned out to parallel workers across different models, with consistency checks and honest failure reporting, so that broad tasks finish faster and partial runs never masquerade as complete.
Acceptance Criteria: SwarmPlanner fans out via asyncio.gather with per-worker cross-model routing, write-conflict fallback to sequential chain, /swarm toggle, and a MAESTRO_SWARM_MAX_WORKERS cap (v1.17.0); folder expansion, live worker lifecycle events, explicit-output merge workers, degraded banners with artifact reconciliation, and single-deliverable fan-out skip shipped through v2.3.0.

Summary: Chain defaults and per-step critic gate
Description: As an interactive user, I want chain mode on by default with a per-step critic gate reviewing each mutating step's delta, so that multi-agent runs are the norm and every code-changing step gets adversarial review.
Acceptance Criteria: Interactive sessions start with chain on via a --chain/--no-chain tri-state default (v1.4.2, fixed v1.17.5); each code-mutating chain step snapshots git HEAD plus a diff baseline before running and is reviewed only on its own delta afterward, honoring the significance filter and the existing --no-critic-gate opt-out (v1.15.3).

Description: As an operator, I want routing to weigh artifact, repo, and memory counts in addition to keywords, so that broad consistency tasks land on models with enough context and reasoning depth.
Acceptance Criteria: orchestrator/load.py raises the task profile to MEDIUM (3+ artifacts or 2+ repos, 64k context) or HIGH (6+ artifacts, 3+ artifacts with 2+ repos, or 25+ memories, 128k and DEEP reasoning) at both per-turn selection and inside pm.handle after memory recall; thresholds are user-editable via routing.load_thresholds and visible in /plan (v1.19.0).

Description: As a user, I want quota-exhausted models circuit-broken with automatic fallback to the next capable model, so that a dead provider credential never dead-ends a turn.
Acceptance Criteria: 401/403/402 or balance/quota errors tag results quota_exhausted; pm.handle marks a session circuit breaker, emits an event, and re-runs on the next cheapest capable model up to 3 fallbacks (v1.20.0); the tag propagates through chain/swarm aggregation and mid-run worker selection (v1.20.1); optional routing.fallback_order gives a deterministic secondary chain.

Summary: Repo picker and GitHub org cloning
Description: As a user running intake prompts from docs-only folders, I want a repo picker that clones single repos or GitHub org multi-selects (private repos included), so that code-dependent analysis points at the real codebase.
Acceptance Criteria: Code-dependent playbook prompts fired in folders without source open the picker with a bounded directory probe (v1.15.4); the org flow lists repos via gh with checkbox selection, gh-authenticated cloning of private repos, and org page URLs redirecting to the org flow (v1.16.0/1.16.2); clone failures surface git's own stderr (v1.15.6).

Description: As an interactive user, I want sessions to survive maestro restarts and execution-style follow-ups to carry the previous turn's recommendations, so that long delegations don't lose context.
Acceptance Criteria: Startup restores the most recent project-scoped session record and natively resumes the backend session with a printed Resuming line (v1.22.2); kimi-cli falls back to a fresh session after resume failures (v1.8.5/1.8.6); execution-intent follow-ups inject the prior turn's last_output as [Previous turn's output - act on this], restored across restarts (v1.22.4); native resumes send a current-task-only prompt instead of duplicating the transcript (v1.20.2).

Description: As a project lead, I want intake/design-phase turns to be read-only enforced and nested repo clones auto-reverted, so that early analysis can't mutate code or leave stray edits.
Acceptance Criteria: Playbook prompts tagged read_only: true merge Write/Edit/Bash into blocked_tools across all runtimes (v1.15.4-adjacent read-only tagging v1.22.0); the clone guard snapshots nested git-repo clones before each turn and auto-reverts tracked modifications while the milestone is a pre-implementation phase, disable with MAESTRO_CLONE_GUARD=off (v1.22.0); single-agent turns carry a sole-agent directive and warn when the prompt's artifact_target file was never produced (v1.20.6).

Description: As a user, I want prompts naming an explicit MCP tool or an external mutation to route straight to a single agent, so that chain/swarm planners don't scatter direct actions into recall steps that never execute them.
Acceptance Criteria: is_direct_action() in orchestrator/chain.py detects explicit MCP tool names or mutation-verb plus external-system combinations and bypasses both planners for a single-step run; ChainPlanner.plan() keeps the same gate as defense-in-depth (v1.22.5).

Summary: Adversarial review layer with enforced gates
Description: As a quality gatekeeper, I want a multi-persona adversarial review layer with a machine-enforced gate ledger, a cross-model panel, and auto-invocation on significant blueprint changes, so that only reviewed artifacts can pass /complete.
Acceptance Criteria: maestro --review runs 7 audit personas with RESULT-line parsing against numeric thresholds and an append-only sha256-keyed ledger; a 3-seat cross-model panel routes E/Q/W/J claims with anonymized ranking and a non-GLM chairman; /complete refuses while the gate is unpassed (v2.0.0). Deep review auto-fires on new artifacts, 150+ line changes, or version-marker edits (v2.1.0); personas seat via the capability router on configured models with reports persisted to .open-maestro/reviews/ and change detection working outside git repos via snapshots (v2.1.4/2.1.5/2.1.11); a calibration harness plants 6 sentinel defect classes to score per-persona recall (v2.0.0).

Description: As a project lead, I want design-document changes to trigger an automatic adversarial artifact-critic pass with a durable review file, so that citation fraud and net-new masquerading are caught per turn.
Acceptance Criteria: Turns creating or modifying a docs/*.md artifact by more than 50 changed lines run the code-critic agent on the artifact and append an APPROVE/WARN/BLOCK verdict (v1.21.0, MAESTRO_ARTIFACT_CRITIC=off); each pass persists a full review to docs/reviews/artifact-critic-<timestamp>.md (v2.5.2); the gate fires outside git repositories using mtime/size snapshots (v2.1.4).

Summary: Mermaid diagram skill and advisory linter
Description: As a design author, I want a codified mermaid diagram skill plus an advisory linter, so that diagrams render valid and decisions live in tables, not graph nodes.
Acceptance Criteria: The mermaid-diagrams skill prescribes the narrowest diagram type, syntax-pitfall rules, render-before-save validation, and .md plus rendered .png outputs, wired into the engineer, data-engineer, and documentation agents (v2.2.0); the standard keeps parked/resolved decisions in companion tables and open gates as inline tags, enforced by a non-blocking review.diagram_lint advisory with a MAESTRO_DIAGRAM_LINT=off kill switch (v2.4.0/2.4.1).

Description: As a user, I want /model and --model pins to resolve the pinned model's runtime through the registry, so that a shorthand like opus seats the turn on the right backend instead of an arbitrary runtime.
Acceptance Criteria: /model opus and --model opus resolve through the registry (id to alias to identifier to fallback table) and seat the turn on that model's runtime; vendor shorthands opus/sonnet/haiku were added to the fallback alias table; OPEN_MAESTRO_RUNTIME now narrows router candidates with a clear error for unknown values (v2.2.0).

Description: As a design author, I want the blueprint-contract skill to codify the design-001 contract shape, citation discipline, and sign-off conventions, so that every drafted contract follows one protocol and freezes only via design-005.
Acceptance Criteria: The skill encodes the draft-not-frozen framing, 9-section contract skeleton, [existing]/[net-new] citation anchors, the UI-value authority ladder, stable DT/OQ/RR register IDs, and mandatory propagation of the decision trail to milestones.yaml, docs/design-decisions.md, and the decision-register CSV (v2.5.0/2.5.1); design-005 absorbed the adversarial verification step as a cross-artifact consistency pass holding the only sign-off verdict that may say frozen (v3.0.0).

Description: As a playbook user, I want prompts to declare after: prerequisites with ANY semantics, so that dependent prompts like adversarial verification appear only once their prerequisites have actually run.
Acceptance Criteria: Prompts support after: <prompt-id> and ungate only when the prerequisite has a run record in prompt history or its artifact exists on disk (v1.21.0); after: accepts a list with ANY semantics so a gated prompt appears once at least one listed prerequisite has run (v2.5.2).

Description: As a project historian, I want a strict status enum, an ADR format, and word budgets on register cells, so that the decision register stays parseable and prose detail lives in design-decisions.md.
Acceptance Criteria: The Status column is a strict 10-value enum with per-status definitions and a post-edit validation snippet (v3.0.0); the skill gains an ADR section (D-n IDs, Proposed/Ratified/Superseded lifecycle, home in docs/design-decisions.md) plus cell budgets of 50 words for Decision and 25 for Context, with over-budget analysis moved to dated design-decisions.md sections referenced from the cell (v3.0.0/3.0.3).

Description: As a playbook operator, I want the milestone prompts' formats codified as reusable skills, so that prompts stay short and a convention change edits one skill instead of nine prompts.
Acceptance Criteria: Eight skills shipped covering the milestone artifacts: intake-synthesis, reuse-assessment, risk-register, epic-breakdown, execution-plan, ux-template-spec, bdd-story-authoring, and traceability-matrix (v3.0.0); the intake/design/build/plan/impl prompts now reference their skills by name and the research, product-owner, documentation, and security agents preload them.

Description: As a project lead editing milestones.yaml by hand, I want authoring governance covering schema, invariants, and gate-as-blocker rules, so that hand edits stay dashboard-safe.
Acceptance Criteria: The skill documents the schema cheat-sheet, the ACTIVE-only two-list invariant, the resolved_at resolution convention, custom-milestone rules (stable id, weight 0 for gates, provenance in notes), atomic-edit discipline, and a validation snippet (v3.0.0); sign-off gates with no deliverables are recorded as blockers on the milestone they gate rather than weight-0 milestones (v3.0.5); mutations go through MCP tools when wired, hand edits as fallback (v3.2.0).

Summary: MCP server and CLI tool allowlists
Description: As an MCP-capable agent (Claude Code, Kimi), I want a maestro MCP server exposing milestone tools with drift-guarded mutations, plus CLI runtimes that respect mcp__ tool allowlists, so that progress is recorded without hand-editing YAML and MCP tools are never silently filtered out.
Acceptance Criteria: maestro --mcp-serve (stdio) exposes get_state, list_blockers, add_blocker, resolve_blocker, and set_milestone_status through a mutations service that refuses saves when the plan file changed on disk; maestro --mcp-init merges the server into .mcp.json without touching existing entries (v3.2.0); mcp__-prefixed tool names pass through claude-cli tool flags with per-server allowlist auto-widening (v1.22.3); a vetted read-only MCP tool set is unioned into restricted auditor seats (v2.2.0).

Description: As a stakeholder reading the dashboard, I want milestone-level progress percentages and weight-aware epic completion, so that percent bars reflect real work remaining rather than flat averages.
Acceptance Criteria: An optional progress field (0-100) on in_progress/blocked milestones replaces the flat 50% while completed stays 100 (v3.1.0); epic and overall completion use the weighted_completion rule over non-skipped milestones, client_ready is true only when every non-skipped milestone is completed, and an all-completed epic reads Complete (v3.1.0).

Description: As a project lead implementing a large story backlog, I want stories batched into bundles run by a 5-step lean process, so that agent rounds and environment checks drop by an order of magnitude.
Acceptance Criteria: The bundle-execution skill defines bundles of roughly 1,500 production lines grouped by repo/stack/touch-point, the 5-step process (kickoff questions before coding, one stacked-branch build pass, one independent review, one fix-and-merge pass, one env checklist per bundle), the bundle-plan doc template, and a rescoping rule that revises bundles rather than story rows (v3.3.0); build-005 authors the plan with total-coverage scoping across every epic and single-doc update-in-place discipline (v3.3.0/3.7.3).

Description: As a product owner, I want UI bundles to declare a visual target and prove fidelity with rendered screenshots, so that what ships matches the approved prototype rather than passing code-level gates alone.
Acceptance Criteria: UI bundle plan rows must open with a filled VISUAL TARGET block and step-1 done-criteria requires 1600x1200 side-by-side screenshots committed under docs/reviews/screens/ for populated/empty/error states (v3.4.0); ux-template-spec gains prototype-reconciliation and verify-against-codebase sections; code-review-standards gains a visual/design-system review section activated on screen-touching diffs; impl-000 lists spec-vs-prototype divergences needing a ruling or CR before coding (v3.4.0).

Description: As an M3 architect, I want a readable client approval brief assembled only after a passing design sign-off, so that clients ratify designs through a signature instrument instead of the raw artifact stack.
Acceptance Criteria: Playbook prompt design-006 assembles docs/client-design-approval.md per the client-design-approval skill: six numbered sections plus reference appendix, named approver with DRAFT banner, explicit-call list, three-value decision status vocabulary with provenance, security-and-data confirm-asks, and a signature block recorded as register row APPROVAL-1 (v3.5.0/3.5.1); a hard gate stops brief assembly unless the design-005 sign-off verdict is Signed off or Signed off with conditions (v3.5.2).

Description: As a Claude user, I want the registry to track the 5.5 family with opus-5-5 as the reasoning alias, sonnet-5-5 as default, and fable-5-1 opt-in, so that capability routing seats premium work on current models instead of retired ones.
Acceptance Criteria: claude-opus-5-5 was registered as the claude-cli reasoning/opus alias with claude-opus-4-7 kept addressable for explicit pins (v3.0.0); claude-sonnet now resolves to claude-sonnet-5-5, the claude-opus shorthand to Opus 5.5, claude-fable-5-1 is registered opt-in with no alias, and the fallback alias table no longer falls back to 2024-era models (v3.6.0).

Description: As a build engineer, I want a dev-env-smoke-test skill with liveness bounds and a smoke-doc contract, so that environment verification can't hang a session or invent URLs.
Acceptance Criteria: The skill supplies target-selection rules (remote shared/ephemeral preferred, blank answer means a bounded discovery pass then stop-and-report), anti-hang liveness rules (one boot plus one retry per service, 30s network timeouts, missing dependencies recorded BLOCKED with evidence and owner), and the docs/dev-smoke-test.md contract with PASS / PASS WITH WORKAROUNDS / BLOCKED verdicts and per-service tables (v3.6.0); build-004 targets the ephemeral preview environment by default (v3.0.2); the smoke doc gains a Deploy path section settling delivery routing per the branch-delivery template (v3.7.7).

Description: As a release engineer, I want standing-branch delivery mechanics codified with relay SHA checks, environment pointers, and a final-merge protocol, so that every project deploys through one invariant pipeline instead of rediscovering it.
Acceptance Criteria: The branch-delivery skill encodes the standing-branch model with branch naming as CI control, the push-deploy-verify loop with relay-branch SHA checks catching conflicted-PR silent failures, per-service per-env GitOps values keys with sha-over-branch precedence, a repo onboarding checklist gating first-time delivery, a final-merge protocol requiring explicit user approval before main, evidence conventions, and the docs/delivery-routing.md config template seeded by the smoke test (v3.7.0).

Summary: Playbook input questions with remembered answers
Description: As a playbook user, I want prompts to declare input questions whose answers are remembered per project and echoed visibly, so that repeated runs don't re-ask and a waiting session is obvious in scrollback.
Acceptance Criteria: Prompt templates support an inputs: list of name/question pairs; answers substitute into {name} tokens and a blank answer becomes a discover-from-repo marker so no raw token reaches the agent (v3.0.2); answers persist to .open-maestro/prompt_inputs.yaml and reappear as bracketed defaults, a loud [maestro] INPUT NEEDED banner precedes blocking questions, and answers read via cooked-mode input so pasted text echoes immediately (v3.7.1/3.7.2).

Description: As a project lead, I want agent kickoff questions to surface interactively with recommendations, tagged lead vs client/M3, so that questions are ruled in seconds instead of piling up as Open register rows around a running build.
Acceptance Criteria: Every kickoff question is asked synchronously in the agent's response, numbered with a recommendation and exactly what it blocks (v3.7.4); client/M3 rulings carry the [INTERNAL - not M3-ratified] marker supporting the provisional-ruling pattern, and only declined questions become Open rows plus an outbox message (v3.7.5); the agent writes .open-maestro/awaiting-input.yaml as its last act and the REPL renders an AGENT AWAITING INPUT recap, collecting rulings one-by-one, as a bulk paste, or declined, with rulings returned through the same session (v3.7.6).

Description: As a user, I want project memory stored as plain Markdown notes via the Basic Memory backend, so that memories stay human-readable, git-committable, and never stranded in a discontinued database format.
Acceptance Criteria: memory/basic_memory_client.py implements recall/enhance/store/ensure_initialized over the bm CLI with JSON output, hybrid semantic search, and content-hash idempotent stores; create_memory_client() honors MAESTRO_MEMORY_BACKEND and otherwise auto-detects bm with kuzu-memory as a legacy fallback behind a backend-agnostic MemoryClient protocol (v3.8.0); scripts/migrate_kuzu_memory.py migrates existing .kuzu-memory databases to Basic Memory notes.
